eeg_quality_flags.description: The EEG is dominated by a large artifact shared across channels: amplitude stays above ~1 mV on most of the 32 channels for at least 10 s, far above normal EEG (~0.05-0.15 mV) and task artifacts such as chewing (~0.3-0.5 mV). Likely a poorly-contacting electrode or cable; the exact cause cannot be recovered from the recording. Exclude this range from EEG analyses.
eeg_quality_flags.evidence: Episode read off the raw EEG: the 10-s rolling median of the per-2-s amplitude jumps from ~0.1 mV to 1-3 mV at the start and falls back below 0.15 mV (and stays there for 60 s) at the end, where an experimenter re-attached a loose electrode (tagged in the report). The headset's own signal-quality reading (EQ_OVERALL) is mostly 0 over the episode, while its contact-quality channels mostly still read 'good'.
